text:
Scorching Suslanger will especially delight lovers of necromancy — these lands are literally teeming with the spawn of sinister magic. Nor will those who enjoy exploring dungeons inhabited by the most incredible creatures be disappointed.

Suslanger is a sun-scorched desert. This small island belongs to the Xadagan Empire. Geographically it is divided into two halves: a lowland, comparatively fertile, and an upland, which is desert. The upland is split in two by a huge Canyon carved by a river that flows into a small lake. There is little land on Suslanger fit for living and farming. The river and the lake are the only large sources of water. To extend the cultivated land at least a little, people have to build irrigation canals and dams. Several settlements lie around the lake. There are almost no settlements in the desert, where a few orc tribes still live — strong and skilled enough to survive alongside the Xadaganians, and clever enough not to provoke them into a major war.

Power in Xadagan is harsh and merciless. A numerous guard punishes the slightest breach of the emperor's decrees, while spies and informers report on every suspicious person. Suslanger is of little economic importance to Xadagan, but it is home to a military academy whose graduates hold prominent posts in the imperial army.

The land of Gipat, where your journey begins, resembles the temperate midlands in summer in its relief and vegetation. Beware of the apparent idyll and look around carefully; remember that Gipat's hostile and treacherous inhabitants are unpredictable! Trolls and goblins, bats, wolves, boars, hares and deer lie in wait for you. There are harpies too, in all their three-dimensional splendour. They are fabulously beautiful, but you must already know their foul temper well. More than once you will have to descend into natural caves, man-made mines and dungeons. Some of the dwellers of those worlds, who have never seen the sun or living people, will stay in your memory for a long time — if you manage to make it back to the surface, of course…

This island belongs to the group of orc islands. Its main population is orcs and goblins. The only village where people live is very small and constantly under threat of destruction. There is also a bandit camp whose members somehow manage to get along with the monsters. There is practically no metal here; people use bone and stone weapons and leather armour. Ruins of an unknown ancient civilization are found all over the island. It is small, and it belongs to none of the states because it is hard to reach and swarms with hostile monsters.

The Kanian Empire had plans to annex this land and had even built a fortress, but after the Cataclysm that split the world apart, the fortress and its garrison were left to fend for themselves. A handful of descendants of that garrison still live on Gipat, constantly fighting the goblins for the right to live.

Lightwood is a land of snowy foothills that somewhat resembles medieval Europe. Most of it is covered with wooded mountains; valleys give way to copses, which in turn pass into dense forests. Almost everything around is snow-white.

Lightwood belongs to the Kanian Empire; its territory is very large and its population sparse. Most of Lightwood is covered with wooded mountains. The climate is cold; snow falls early and lies for a long time. There are practically no large towns — even the capital of Lightwood is more of a big village, a cluster of two- and three-storey wooden houses. The other settlements, proudly called towns, look even more like overgrown villages.

The main occupations of the people of Lightwood are logging, hunting, and mining ore and gold. People usually live in small groups and treat strangers with suspicion and hostility. The inhabitants of Lightwood are freedom-loving and independent by nature. At the slightest hint of a threat they take up arms without hesitation and defend their interests without wasting time on inquiries. Lightwood is ruled by a governor sent from the capital, but his power can hardly be called absolute. The provinces enjoy considerable autonomy, which the Council does not curtail without reason. Everything there is decided by the local authorities, so every village has its own ways...

At some unknown time the sorcerer Firez, banished by the surviving June for necromancy, tried to seize the allod of Jigran, bringing with him the power of the Xadagan Empire. He enslaved the June and surrounded the allod with a magical barrier that hid Jigran from everyone, including the curse of the June. But the spells did irreparable damage to the allod. All the strength drained out of the island, the vegetation withered, the animals died out. Firez raised the beasts and, turning them into zombies, put them into his service. Meanwhile the dying land yielded very poor harvests, and the people of Kania could barely hold back the onslaught of Firez's army.

Jigran had long been a province of Kania. Fortresses were built here and farms established. With the coming of Firez and his all-destroying spells the land stopped bearing fruit, and the fortresses turned from settlements into military camps that barely held out against the pressure of the undead. The largest town, Dar Leanos, is the capital of Kanian Jigran. Here stands the portal from Lightwood, and here live Baron Virill and most of the soldiers.

To the south-west lies the fortress of Dar Ulgorn, which has changed hands more than once. Xadagan settlements stretch to the west. In the far west stand two fortresses: the northern one is the stronghold of Firez himself, the southern one serves as a prison for June scholars. There is also a crossing — ruins of what was once either a fortress or a town, now inhabited by Firez's men and the undead. Jigran is an island of war where no one stays on the sidelines, so there is not a single settlement here that is peaceful and takes no part in the war. Kanian villages die out one after another after attacks by the undead, harpies and other creatures. There is only one man who lives apart: Uncle Rad, a seller of sweets and, at the same time, a spy for Baron Virill. His tent stands east of the fortress of Dar Ulgorn.

Geographically, the allod of Yazes is divided into several regions, each with its own climate. The western part of the island is taken up by a forest (mostly oak groves) called the Ancient Forest. To its south-west lie the Lost Lakes, a mysterious land whose peoples do not obey the crown of Yazes. Formally the Ancient Forest is part of the kingdom, but its true masters are the druids. In addition, the elven city of Elliavan stands in the north-west of the allod. The south and south-east of Yazes are desert (most of it called the Hemer Desert), inhabited mainly by orc and goblin tribes united into several clans. Accordingly, the central and north-eastern parts of the allod are the territory of the kingdom of Yazes proper, populated mostly by humans.

The allod of Umoir, the first to be surrounded by a magical protection against the Astral, is the largest island-shard of Sarnaut. The allod abounds in small villages, forests, lakes and all kinds of wildlife, and at its very centre stands the tower of the Great Mage Skrakan.

Geography:
The climate of the allod is warm and pleasant; everything grows here, and the lush groves are ample proof of it. High mountains can be found in the north, but on the whole plains prevail. The allod is very large, so several forests spread across it at once, the largest of which is Rotwood.

Inhabitants
Most of the allod's population are humans, living in many villages and in the large city of Plagot. The city boasts a rich tavern where travellers, dashing mercenaries and other folk gather, a school of magic and trading shops. Formally the allod of Umoir belongs to no state, but thanks to its mysterious sealing both empires took a keen interest in it, and Skrakan's leaning towards the Kanians and his firm friendship with Tensess are common knowledge.

[Map missing]

Forox is one of the main Kanian allods, alongside Kania and Umoir.

This land is the birthplace of the Great Mage Aidenus, who held the allod together against the destructive force of the Astral during the Cataclysm. After Aidenus began holding Kania, the Great Mage Bogsha — evidently a disciple of Aidenus — settled in Rakhl-Forox, the Tower of the Great Mage of Forox. It was thanks to Bogsha's efforts that the people elected Ivan the Ascetic, a priest of the Church of Light, as Governor. Under him the Church of Light gained enormous power on Forox, and the allod itself effectively became the Church's domain. Unfortunately, Bogsha went missing in the Misty Valley of Forox, after which the allod came to be held by his disciple, Tritogor. From the words of Tritogor's own disciple, Wienna, we learn that "something dark took hold of Tritogor's mind", and under his rule Forox was nearly emptied of people.

[Map missing]

Grok is a vast steppe; small forests and mountains are found only at the edges of the island.

Originally the allod belonged to the elves of the House de Vevre (in the days before the League existed), who had several small towns here. The local steppes are not very fertile: there are few rivers and cold winds often blew, so grain did not grow well. Magic helped the elves in this, and besides magic they found another solution — raising all kinds of livestock.

Besides the elves, orcs lived in the steppes a little beyond the centre of the allod. The House de Vevre would of course have liked to be rid of the orcs — but how do you chase them across the steppe?

Claude de Vevre, the Great Mage of Grok, once tried to teach the orc Rodogor magic (for it was here that Lorzub the Fierce, the Legendary Orc, was born), making him his disciple, but these efforts bore no fruit: the orcs proved incapable of magic. The angered Rodogor turned to Nezeb, the Great Mage of Igsh and leader of Xadagan.

In the year 707 of the New Era, the orcs and the Xadaganians captured Grok, killing Claude de Vevre, the Great Mage of the allod. Nezeb kept the promise he had made to Rodogor, and a Xadagan Great Mage began holding the allod.

[Map missing]

The Gibberlings called their small continent Isa — "the island" — and grew used to thinking of the sea as their native element and of a ship as their home.

There was a place on Isa sacred to all Gibberlings: a place where the realms of ice and fire meet, where the Great Tree grows, from whose branches, legend has it, the first Gibberlings, As and Emla, were made.

Along with the Gibberlings, Isa was also home to the Praiden and to tribes of wild orcs.

This continent was lost in the Cataclysm, shattering into pieces. One of those shards is Howlem.

[Map missing]

Kech is an allod that was once Kanian and was later captured by the Empire. Kech was the second allod, after Grok, to be attacked by the combined forces of the orcs and the Xadaganians. In 725 the allod was captured by the Empire, which had to fight on two fronts — here and on the allod of Grok, which the League, in the person of the Kanians and the elves who had concluded a military alliance against the Empire, was trying to win back.

[Map missing]

The only allod where the orcs could feel more or less, as they say, "at home" was the allod of Izune, which survived thanks to the presence of the Great Dragoness Soliskar: being a magical creature, she held the allod back from being swallowed by the Astral by the very fact of her existence. Several orc tribes, feuding with one another, survived here. True, a mage soon arrived from Xadagan, and the dragoness had to leave Izune. It was here that Rodogor became Supreme Shaman.

[Map missing]

It belongs to the Empire and is populated by the Zem: even before the Cataclysm, the land from which the allod formed was the centre of their empire. It is held by one of the Great Mages of the Zem (for a time it was held by Nefer Ur himself). The climate is desert.

[Map missing]

On Scarge itself many wonders can be seen — mechanical horses, miracle-working idols, each with clicking cogs and turning keys. For a time the Great Mage of the allod was Catherina. The allod was destroyed during the Night of Astral Portals.

[Map missing]

Ovus is a Kanian allod. Its present location, territorial allegiance and other information are unknown. Xadagan planned an invasion of Ovus around 702 of the New Era, but after meeting Rodogor, Nezeb changed his plans.

The island of Clement de Desirae (possibly the island of the emigrants, but in the League quests it is referred to precisely as Clement's Island) is the allod where the League storyline begins. It shows what happens when the Great Mage who holds an allod is killed.

[Map missing]

Yakhch was once an ordinary desert allod, but it was here that the druids came in their time, having decided to try planting a seed of the Great Tree in one of the oases. The Tree changed the landscape of Yakhch profoundly. Where there was desert, mighty forests — a true taiga — now rise. The climate changed too: there is more rain and it is colder overall. Today this land is a source of timber, which the Xadaganians ship to various parts of their state.

[Map missing]

Ark was originally a small principality in the far south-west of Kania. Nezeb's conquest, when he unleashed the hordes of Ugr on the southern borders, passed it by, but at the same time cut it off from the main body of Kanian lands. Erast himself considered himself independent, yet showed Nezeb various signs of respect — he was, after all, the nearest neighbour. The Xadagan emperor did not dare touch Ark either: the profits from trade were considerable, and simply seizing such a scrap of land would bring no benefit. If you were to choose a place to live as you please, Ark could well be it. Neither Kania nor Xadagan collects taxes or recruits troops there; live and let live. Besides, there were no threats on Ark at all… except perhaps a few trolls and kobolds in the mountain caves, but they did not risk coming down into the valley. And the people of Ark, of course, are cheerful. Kanians and Xadaganians have mixed here so long ago that you cannot tell one from the other. Elves lived in these lost lands too — the House de Ark.

[Map missing]

The Great Mage of this allod was the wise Gramon de Doucer, a disciple of the elven mages of old, second in power only slightly to Skrakan. He united everyone who found themselves on his allod after the Night of Woe into a single, largest House, and revived the tradition of the Great Houses, in which the remaining Eight Great Houses now began to take part. Yoggor itself is a rather unusual place: a majestic forest full of enormous trees. Most of the elves live in their own castles, scattered in great numbers across the allod. Although only elves inhabit this allod, there are also those who can pose a threat to lone travellers — various mindless creatures such as giant spiders and mantises. But everything comes to an end, and a terrible fate befell Yoggor too: an extraordinarily deadly spell that changed the familiar way of life on the allod, darkening it with gloom. After the deadly spell, it changed its name to Nocturne.

Malar is a League allod inhabited by Kanians and by the elves of the lesser House de Amfas, known for its reverent attitude to etiquette.

[Map missing]

Ellanesh is an elven allod, the hidden abode of the lesser House de Fore, whose members are the most famous sybarites and hedonists in all of Sarnaut. On their allod the elves of the House de Fore are constantly occupied with indulging in the most refined way of life — tasting the rarest delicacies, listening to the most beautiful music, studying the most thrilling arts of love…
[Map missing]

[Map missing]

Anga is a League allod, the homeland of Pelagiy Guslarov, the first of the storytellers of the allod of Anga, who collects ancient tales and byliny and performs chastushki.
[Map missing]

[Map missing]

Lumenara is the elven allod of the Great House de Ardeur: a shining beacon in the abyss of the Astral, an amber-lit refuge for all who are eager to change this world. Thanks to Renard, this allod has now received all the latest elven technical inventions, and the power of the Light has made it a truly safe place. Besides the elves, Lumenara is home to a tribe of Aviaks who have become their loyal servants, protectors and helpers. It is also the abode of the lesser House de Gloire.

[Map missing]

Gelida is the elven allod of the Great House de Blizare: a very frosty place, but thanks to elven potions the elves know no hardship. It is always warm in their palaces, even when a snowstorm rages outside the window. Besides the elves, tribes of Forestfolk live on Gelida. The elves have taught them a great deal, and in return received their boundless loyalty and devotion. It is also the abode of the lesser House de Ruse, which provides food for the elves from the snowy forests, rich in game, and the lakes full of fish.

The Free City, located on the allod of Tortuga, was an early concept (of Allods Online) conceived as a centre of piracy. Very early work on it was found in the game files; the idea was eventually abandoned.

The city was laid out in an arc, forming the shape of a gulf or bay. In the middle was a pier, behind it buildings, and higher still a Central building with a balloon. A Lighthouse presumably stood at the centre of the bay. The city had three tiers.
[Map missing]

Kania. The main allod of the League. Its native population is Kanians and, strangely enough, Zem — though the Zem on Kania could not come back to life properly and are mindless undead. The allod is home to the capital of the League, Novograd, as well as the cursed castle of the Valir dynasty, one of Tep's pyramids and the Great Tree. The climate is temperate in places and tundra in others.
Igsh. The main allod of the Empire. The climate is predominantly desert. Its native population is Xadaganians and Zem. The allod is home to the capital of the Empire, Nezebgrad.

Holy Land. The allegiance of the allod is disputed: not only do the League and the Empire fight over it, but part of the allod has also been seized by the goblin mafia. Its native population is human. Every possible kind of climate is represented. It is distinguished by a pyramid of Tep in which dwells the Spark of Tensess (the very one who granted everyone immortality). Because of this, some artefacts of the Zem people (that is, the ancient ones, from before Tep killed everyone) became saturated with holy magic and acquired unexpected but extremely powerful properties. Then Sarn's cultists and their demons meddled, and the artefacts' properties became more unexpected still.
[Map missing]

Coldberg. It belongs to the Free Traders. The climate is tundra. It is run by the Gibberling oligarch Sigurd the Swindler. It exists thanks to the large amount of meteorite iron in its depths, which is sold to both the League and the Empire.

Avilon. The allod belongs to the Historians' faction and is held by their leader, the Great Mage Zayan. The climate is temperate. After the start of the Allods Online storyline it is attacked by demons and Sarn's cultists, supported by a huge flying galleon-ship built by the Great Mage Gorluxor. By the end of the storyline the attack has been repelled, and the ship captured; the Historians now use it.

Dragon Ring. In fact it is an archipelago of small allods. The climate is tropical. It belongs, as you might easily guess, to the descendants of the last surviving dragons. Its native population is lizards and the draconids stamped out of them. At first it was thought to be held by a dragoness named Soliskar, but she later flew off on her own business while the archipelago remained. So this archipelago apparently exists either thanks to meteorite iron or thanks to some artefact.

Yazes. Originally an imperial allod. The second game of the series ("Allods 2: Master of Souls") takes place on it. After the first demon attack it was shattered into shards. At the start of Allods Online, one of the largest shards is used as a base by Sarn's cultists. The climate was originally varied; afterwards it is impossible to determine because of the multitude of demons, who have turned it into a rocky desert. The tower of the Great Mage Gorluxor also stands on it.

Yazes. Originally an imperial allod. The second game of the series ("Allods 2: Master of Souls") takes place on it. After the first demon attack it was shattered into shards. At the start of Allods Online, one of the largest shards is used as a base by Sarn's cultists. The climate was originally varied; afterwards it is impossible to determine because of the multitude of demons, who have turned it into a rocky desert. The tower of the Great Mage Gorluxor also stands on it.

Kingdom of Elements. The allod is contested by the League and the Empire. It was discovered in the Astral at the end of the Allods Online storyline. Every possible type of climate is represented on the allod. What holds it together is unknown.

Kingdom of Nature. The allod is contested by the League and the Empire. Its location in the Astral is unknown — only pagans (shamans, druids and the like) can reach it, by means of a special ability. Every possible type of climate is represented on the allod. What holds it together is unknown.

Isle of Revelation. The main allod of the Master's Attendants. It is one of the shards of Gipat. Its climate is hard to determine, since it is almost entirely covered with the ruins of a June city, but it is most likely temperate. It holds the cave of the last June mage, Tka-Rik.

Star Gates (Battle of the Gods raid)

text: Gipat. Once one of the last dwelling places of the June race. At the start of the Allods Online storyline it had split into many shards. The largest shards exist by the will of Nihaz (one is called the Gipat Shard, the other the Isle of Revelation — more on it below) and serve to reveal the truth about Sarnaut and Sarn. The climate on the Gipat Shard is temperate. A small islet near the allod is used by Nihaz's servants to house the Whirlpool of Time, a device for travelling into the past (and possibly into the future). Among the smaller shards of Gipat, Allods Online also features the Wandering Island, the Twilight Isle, the Dead City and the Frozen Peak.

Irdrich. An allod once kept in the Astral by a Great Mage (name unknown) who had locked himself in a time loop. It was later captured by Tep's cultists. It is notable for the newest of the pyramids built, the base of Tep's cultists and a huge complex for creating virtual reality. The climate was originally tropical; since Tep's capture it cannot be determined.
The Pearl Ring is an illusory reflection of Irdrich created by Sihal, Tep's henchman.

An island near the Pearl Ring, close to the Rainbow Atoll. On the island is a camp of anarchist Aviaks. The camp has a forge, a storehouse, a headquarters, a kitchen, a barracks and the anarchists' huts.

Umoir. Formally it belongs to the League, in fact it is neutral. It is under the rule of the Great Mage Catherina. The climate is mostly temperate, desert in places. Its native population is Kanians and elves — though by the start of the storyline the elves had been driven off to a small neighbouring allod. Umoir was formerly ruled by the Great Mage Skrakan. It is marked by an epidemic of a disease called the Plague, which transforms every living thing. It later turned out that Sarn was behind the spread of the disease, but by the end of the storyline the disease has not gone anywhere — it has simply stopped spreading. The allod is notable for the ruins of a city from the first game in the series ("Allods: Rage of Mages"), Plagot, and for the barrow where a demon from that same first game of the universe is buried. On top of that, a large community of pagans lives on the allod, worshipping, among other gods, the daughter of the God of Darkness — Klavdia.

It is considered the largest allod of Sarnaut.
In the days of 5.0

A quiet little island, an unremarkable one. Seven hero brothers once lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there, having fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a present: a wondrous mirror, the work of the ancient June, with a golden frame and a glass of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that: from them you can only expect some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it is downright frightening. Although... what if there are hunters willing to get that mirror? For the brave, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

Oh, Boyar Jeer is a living legend! Though "living" depends on how you look at it... He is a necromancer, one of the best in the world. Some even say he is a Great one! Whether that's the truth or idle talk, I don't know: for many years now he has lived alone on his estate, talking only with the dead. His peasants are another matter: cheerful, talkative, and not poor either — if the goods are good, they always have a coin to spare. Though a merchant I know was there recently and told me something strange. He steps off the ship, lays out his wares, and the peasants don't so much as glance his way: they all stand stock-still, staring at one point. He looked closer and saw what seemed like a ghostly mist hanging over them all... He took to his heels right away! Whether it's true or not, I don't know — I sell it as I bought it! If you happen to be there — maybe you'll find out the truth?

This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, an oligarch and inventor. He is a rich and famous man, but not much respected: he is far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only this last time he picked the wrong target: he had the nerve to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker would not swallow the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. Nothing came of it, I think: the imperial soldiers are strong, but a factory stuffed to the rafters with weapons can't be taken in one rush either. We Leaguers have nothing to do there — except perhaps watch the show from afar. Want to make a bet? I wager ten gold that the Imperials won't manage it!

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's not to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with the technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they wanted to open the gates, I don't know, and where they did open them, I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the staff were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly off-limits. Want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you do love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... well, maybe just in a low voice, in my ear.

Ney is not a very large allod, although it was here that Zayan, together with Skrakan, first succeeded in creating the holding ritual. It lies in the middle of a plain that was once far up in the mountains. The local landmark deserves a mention too — Rakhl-Ney, a tower that is almost the only building on the allod. The Council of Historians now sits in it. The tower itself is a grandiose library, with shelves the size of several houses. Of course, not only books are kept in Rakhl-Ney; there are plenty of artefacts of all kinds here as well. Besides the tower, the sights include an old system of portals leading to a great many allods. This was something like a crossroads where many magical paths of the June tribe converged… It is only a pity that many of the portals no longer work.

For as long as I've been ploughing the Astral, this islet was always just a frozen lump of rock — no life, no vegetation. And recently it changed as if by magic: now streams flow there, trees blossom, and there are even some little houses! I put in to shore, and more wonders — creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Like Gibberlings, but not Gibberlings, fluffy and long-eared. They are friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they are afraid their kin might go to war against them. I wished them the help of the Light, and they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. A riddle, not an island, honestly!

This place is well known — it has a bad name all across the Astral. The foremost pirate nest in the world! What bandits and cutthroats aren't there! Feint the Greedy himself moved there shortly before his death — they say he buried his treasure there too... Well, anyone can wag their tongue about pirate treasure. But the fresh rumours about that island are far worse. They say someone has finally found a way to deal with the buccaneers. A gentleman of fortune I know wanted to stop there and sell off his loot, but then he looks — smoke rising in a column, the fort in ruins, and above it what seem like bluish tentacles as thick as a mast swaying... In short, a decent person had no business there before, and now even less so!

I've been to this island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... A settlement stands there — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it's pleasant to visit and you can trade at a profit. They say, though, that some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they're not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries for help. Or maybe you'll help them, show some heroism?

Until recently this rich mine belonged to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in fact the Mistress lives in the depths of the island to this day. If she wants, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. And so she stopped wanting to. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her respect, but now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are, of course, countless — only she guards them so well that you can't get near them!

Ferris. At the start of the Allods Online storyline the allod is neutral; by its end it is occupied by the League and the Empire. Its native population is the savage Tungars. Before the storyline began, the allod housed an imperial research base, "Project Gates", which studied the construction of a portal to other worlds and one of the captured inhabitants of such another world (and, on top of that, the modification of living beings, the creation of mechanoids and the study of cloning). But the otherworlder proved unexpectedly powerful and managed to turn almost all the inhabitants of the base into monsters, who slaughtered the rest. Only a cultist of Tep who had infiltrated the project's leadership survived, and at the end of the Allods Online storyline he is still running around somewhere in the basements of the laboratory complex. Cloning was first invented right here, though the technology did not reach the Empire at the time. How Sarn's cultists managed to obtain it is unclear.

Dane. A neutral allod with a temperate climate. The allod is run by the oligarch Ivan Chelezny. It is home to one of the Demon Hunters' fortresses, called the "White" one, two large towns and an ancient elven palace. It is populated mostly by humans.

Ammer. An allod formed on the site of the battle (and death) of Sarn and the Architect. It is distinctive in that its shape resembles a statue. The climate on the allod is temperate. It is home to the Aoidoi race. In the Astral near the allod live demons of the latest generation, as well as demons neutral towards the living. Near the allod lies an islet with an observatory — a complex for travelling into the past and the future.

Sogot. The main allod of the demonologists. Sarn originally used it for experiments on demons, so its climate is impossible to determine: the whole allod is covered with an unbroken layer of demon bones that have piled up there almost since the Cataclysm. For a time it was captured by the Demon Hunters, who even managed to build one of their citadels on it. But then the demons took the allod back.

Once the elves had a single kingdom — Irene. After the fall of the June nothing could compare with the might of this kingdom, in which even the lowliest vagabond wielded magic. Striving to become stronger still, the elite of this elven kingdom delved ever deeper into hitherto unexplored realms of magic. The elves' attention was drawn to the mysterious magic of the June — blood magic. Using the rituals of blood magic, some elves became vampires and were doomed to an eternal thirst that could only be quenched with the blood of others. These events became known as the "Blood Feast". The problem was eventually brought under control, but it did not pass without a trace for Irene: trust among the elves was shattered. Many of them left the kingdom, settling in various hidden corners of Yul. A little later the elves began to form Houses — families, each of which lived by its own laws and rules.

Suslanger. It belongs to the Empire. The climate is desert. Its native inhabitants are Xadaganians. Construction of the "Gates-3" facility has begun. The island has opened to free visits and been declared a peaceful zone; now you can see Gibberlings relaxing under the hot wind and the blazing sun, Kanian recruits in the ranks of the local pioneers, while Zem scholars freely exchange their knowledge with elven engineers.
